subject: SLA: Temporary Degradation Tolerance & Monthly Smoothing Proposal
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@starlattice.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@starlattice.com
Date: 2026-12-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial ask — tolerance for short degradation windows

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we move toward contract language, procurement is pushing back on the rigid monthly uptime target because our workload has well-known bursty periods. They asked whether Redwood can include a temporary degradation tolerance that smooths monthly credits when a small number of short-duration degradations occur during cloud migrations.

High-level request from Starlattice:
- Allow up to three short degradations (<= 30 minutes each) per month to be excluded from the credit calculation provided they coincide with documented maintenance or customer-initiated cutovers.
- For incidents outside maintenance windows, apply a smoothing rule: convert cumulative short degradations (<6 hours total) into a single remediation band with a reduced credit multiplier.

Can you propose wording we can share with procurement? Attaching a usage pattern CSV for reference.

Best,
Nora
Procurement | Starlattice Inc.

Attachments: starlattice-service-patterns.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: Nora Patel <nora@starlattice.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-09T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — tolerance for short degradation windows

Nora — thanks for the clear ask and the sample traces. Ben and Laura looped in to confirm operational impact. High-level response below; I attached a short proposal PDF that has specific contract language and examples.

Proposed approach (summary):
1) Maintenance carve-out: Planned maintenance windows documented in advance (>=72 hours notice) will not count toward the monthly uptime calculation.
2) Temporary degradation tolerance: Up to three unplanned degradations of 30 minutes or less may be excluded if they meet post-incident evidence requirements (trace, start/end timestamps, and operator notes).
3) Smoothing rule for small cumulative impact: If total unplanned degraded time in a month is less than 6 hours and none of the events breach P99 latency by >3x, we will apply a smoothing factor that reduces the monthly credit by 50% of the standard formula.

Operational safeguards we suggest:
- Incident evidence collection checklist (included in PDF).
- One-time kickoff period (first month after go-live) where both sides gather telemetry to validate thresholds.
- A maximum cap on monthly credits for accounts under 1M tokens/day to avoid disproportional remediation charges.

Next steps: Ben, can you confirm whether the smoothing multiplier and evidence checklist are acceptable operationally? Laura, happy to have you review contract phrasing before I send back to Nora.

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-12-09_redwood-sla-delta-proposal.pdf (PDF, 38KB)
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-10T09:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Re: Initial ask — tolerance for short degradation windows

Irene / team — quick ops check. From an implementation standpoint we're comfortable with the maintenance carve-out and the evidence checklist. Notes:
- We can automate collection of start/end timestamps and P95/P99 deltas for the evidence bundle; that reduces manual validation.
- The 6-hour cumulative threshold is reasonable but recommend we change the smoothing multiplier to 40% (i.e., reduce the credit by 40% of the standard formula) to better align with historical impact on token billing.
- Recommend excluding edge cases where capacity exhaustion (customer burst >5x baseline sustained for >1hr) caused the degradation — those should still be credit-eligible.

Irene — if procurement accepts the 40% smoothing, we can bake the exact telemetry fields into the contract exhibit.

Ben
Director, Reliability Engagement | Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. Procurement reviewed and asked for two clarifications before they can sign off:
1) Can the monthly cap language be explicit? They want an explicit ceiling expressed as a percentage of monthly invoice (e.g., credits cannot exceed 25% of the monthly service fee unless agreed by both parties).
2) For the evidence checklist, they want a maximum 7-business-day window to submit post-incident evidence to qualify for exclusion.

They are okay with the concept of smoothing but asked whether Redwood is willing to accept the 40% multiplier Ben suggested.

Would Redwood accept: smoothing multiplier = 40%, max monthly credit cap = 25% of invoice, evidence submission window = 7 business days? If so we can get procurement legal to draft the redlines.

Best,
Nora

Subject: Final position: temporary-tolerance + caps + evidence window

Nora / procurement team — thank you for the fast turnaround. After internal review we can accept the three clarifications with one small adjustment:
- Smoothing multiplier: agree to 40%.
- Monthly cap: agree to a hard cap equal to 25% of the monthly invoice for the first 12 months post-activation. After month 12, cap reverts to standard account-level cap in section 5.1. This gives both sides predictability during early production.
- Evidence window: agree to a 7-business-day submission window; Redwood will prioritize evidence review within 5 business days once submitted.

Additional operational items to include in contract exhibit:
- A short example table showing how three 20-minute degradations in a month would be evaluated (included in PDF).
- A single escalation path to Redwood CS for disputed exclusions (email + 72-hour SLA for initial review).

If that aligns, Laura will include the exact clause language and Ben will confirm the telemetry field names for the exhibit. We can then accept procurement's redlines and prepare a DocuSign for signature.

Next steps:
- Laura to send contract-ready clause by EOD 2026-12-17.
- Ben to post a brief telemetry spec to the shared Docsend by 2026-12-16.
- Nora to confirm procurement legal readiness to receive redlines.

Thanks all — looking forward to getting this over the line.
